s.how: Cook 3 sliced onions slowly with a spoon of brown sugar and thyme for 30 minutes. Cut shortcrust into rounds and press into a patty tin. Bake at 190C for 12 minutes, then fill with the onions and a piece of goat's cheese and bake 5 more minutes.

s.note: Bridget's capers in her birthday menu
s.how: Slice a baguette and toast until golden. Spread with cream cheese, top with folds of smoked salmon, a scatter of capers and a little lemon zest. Serve on a plate at a dinner party where at least one thing will go badly.

m.note: the leek soup that turns blue from the string
m.how: Slice 3 leeks and soften in 60g butter with 500g diced potatoes for 10 minutes without browning. Add 1L chicken stock and simmer 25 minutes until the potato is very soft. Blend until smooth, stir in 150ml cream and season with salt and white pepper. Fry thin strips of the green leek tops in hot oil until crisp, and blitz chives with 3 tbsp olive oil. Serve the soup with a swirl of cream, the chive oil, crispy leeks and buttered crusty bread. Tie the leeks with kitchen twine, not blue string.

w.note: the orange marmalade on Bridget's birthday menu
w.how: Spoon 4 tbsp orange marmalade into a greased pudding basin. Beat 125g butter with 125g sugar, add 2 eggs and fold in 175g self-raising flour. Spoon on top, cover tightly and steam for 90 minutes. Turn out and serve with hot custard.

d.note: Bridget's diary, alcohol units counted daily
d.how: Slice 2 ripe peaches and 1 orange into a big jug. Add 750ml chilled chardonnay, 200ml peach nectar and 2 tbsp honey and stir. Chill for at least 1 hour. Fill 4 wine glasses with ice and fruit from the jug, pour in the sangria and top with a splash of soda water. For non-drinkers, swap the wine for sparkling apple juice.
